summary: Nine inactive proofs extend the curve-submersion model construction across critical fibers. Potential descent, a Rouche image estimate for Lelong pullback, all-weight ideal types, L1 pullback and analytic restriction supply the foundations. A constant Gauduchon pushforward gives exact polar traces, Borel restriction and total variation, including fiber multiplicities. For a positive base form, the full model space retains the complete curve metric, analytic closure, nearest ideal retraction and all-obstacle atomic criterion.
manual_obligations: Nonconstant p on connected X has a proper analytic critical set with finitely many compact irreducible components.
The differential vanishes on each component smooth locus; its base image is one point, so the critical-value set is finite.
Regular fibers are compact and connected; the corrected psh potential is constant on each, including an entirely minus-infinity fiber.
The submersion argument is used locally with compact fibers, not with a falsely compact punctured total space.
Base upper bounds allow removable extension of corrected subharmonic functions; pullback agrees almost everywhere and hence canonically everywhere.
Surjectivity preserves suprema and ordinary order; disk pullback gives the exact smooth-background lower bound.
The holomorphic germ has finite positive order e; its leading nonzero homogeneous term is detected on a line.
Rouche on the line shows the image of B_r contains a disk of radius c r^e, while the Taylor bound puts it in a disk of radius M r^e.
The ordered three suprema have the same logarithmic-slope limit, with the negative denominator handled by squeezing.
The Lelong calculation applies at every source point of every local modification, with the positive order of the composite.
The accepted local valuative input gives preservation and reflection of all-weight sheaf inclusions and equality; individual ideal extension at a fixed weight is not asserted.
Identity modifications and surjectivity reflect the base Lelong inequalities; smooth curve modifications are isomorphisms.
Hartogs and almost-everywhere order imply convergence of base suprema under fixed-background L1 convergence.
Normalized pullbacks are compact in L1; product charts identify every subsequential limit away from the analytic inverse critical set.
The inverse critical set has smooth volume zero; uniqueness of every subsequential limit gives global L1 pullback.
Analytic presentations compose with a nonconstant open curve map without becoming identically minus infinity.
A generic line germ factors as a local biholomorphic coordinate to the e-th power; analytic restriction gives rational coefficient r.
Every small base coordinate has an e-th root, so bounded error upstairs gives coefficient r/e downstairs, including r=0.
The Green-kernel bound constructs a mean-zero potential for an arbitrary finite positive base measure, not only atomic trace data.
Local harmonic ambiguity does not change the pulled-back current; uniqueness of mean-zero Poisson solutions gives linearity.
The Gauduchon pushforward is a positive harmonic (0,0) distribution and therefore a positive constant, identified on regular fibers.
Smooth approximating measures keep total mass; normalized compactness plus mean zero gives L1 convergence of their potentials.
L1 pullback makes the pulled-back currents and smooth Hermitian traces converge weakly, proving the pushforward identity for all finite measures.
The pushforward identity gives inverse-image Borel carriers, proving restriction without assuming a closed pole set.
Disjoint Jordan carriers remain disjoint upstairs; their masses give exact total variation.
Poincare-Lelong identifies pullback of a point with the fiber divisor including its scheme multiplicities.
Potential and ideal competitor bijections, and openness of p, commute with upper regularization at critical points.
Positive beta makes global maximum truncations admissible; base smooth approximants have pulled-back Hessian rank at most one even at critical points.
Bounded product continuity and every representative descent make all top measures and both singularity volumes zero.
Borel restriction transports the entire polar measure, including its nonatomic part, and gives an exact curve model isometry.
Curve classification gives complete geodesics, diameter 2A, closed atomic subspace and the unique nearest 1-Lipschitz ideal retraction.
Every analytic model is ideal; positive BASE-mass analytic curve models give density, while their upstairs top masses are zero.
Curve metric convergence and the new L1 pullback lemma prove convergence without a false smooth base density at critical values.
Convex stretching competitors descend even at common poles; the arbitrary-smooth-background obstacle-reprojection input handles all upstairs obstacles.
